ruling.recommended_action: Human review: the record cannot settle whether the rider was validly notified of the surge increase — the in-app notice is timestamped 17:14:45 and offers "free cancellation until 17:13", an already-expired option, and the policy-state comparison needed to test the ruling against precedent DISP-2026-0142 ($3.20) is unresolved. Obtain the notification transcript/push-delivery record (was it on screen before trip start at 17:16:00?), verify the rider_notified flag, and confirm the booking-fee/surgeable-subtotal treatment before a differential is paid. Flag the surge notice defect to the pricing team.
ruling.reasoning:
Fare-only case: quote $16.26 at 1.0×, actual $21.14 at 1.4×, rider claims the $4.88 difference. No route issue — actual 5.6 km vs optimal 5.645 km, so deviation is negative and RD is out. The whole difference comes from surge: recompute the trip on the quote base (base 3.90 + distance 7.90 + time 2.25 = 14.05, ×1.0 + booking 1.47 = 15.52) vs the charged (14.05 × 1.4 + 1.47 = 19.67 + 1.47 = 21.14). The $5.62 = 0.4 × 14.05 is the pure surge differential; the quoted total exceeds quote-base + booking by $0.74, so the fare tables as given do not fully reconcile, which is why the exact refund amount (SURGE-3) cannot be mechanically fixed on these figures.

The decisive issue is valid notice (SURGE-1). The record's own notice text fails on two of the three required items: it states the new multiplier (1.4×, OK) but the revised fare given is $22.48, not the $21.14 actually charged, and the "free cancellation until 17:13" is already in the past when the notice was sent at 17:14:45 and before the 17:16:00 trip start — an impracticable, expired option is not a real option to cancel without penalty. A rider cannot be said to have accepted a surcharge in exchange for a cancellation right she never had. The driver's statement that "the app told her the new multiplier, the new fare and that she could cancel for free" is a claim contradicted by the system text (system records override statements). Moreover the notice timestamped 17:14:45 is still only 75 s before trip start and after the surge activated at 17:14:20 — late notice under RD-5's system rule. The only chat log (17:14:10, 17:14:50) shows no rider acknowledgement of the surcharge before riding.

TH-3 confidence: complete = yes (GPS, fare, chat, surge log, telemetry all present); clear = no, the notice item fails on content and the differential cannot be computed unambiguously from the reconciled tables (mixed/opaque base); aligned = questionable, since on a clean reading the outcome would be refund_partial of the surge differential, matching DISP-2026-0142 (~$3.20). Credibility and profile facts do not decide this case. With the ruling turning on a textual finding the records contradict and an arithmetic gap, I escalate rather than rule, per TH-4's no-presumption principle; missing/defective records favour neither side. No safety indicators in any chat, the complaint or the driver statement (no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation) — this is a pricing dispute, not a safety one.
ruling.escalation_reason: Surge notice is defective on content (revised fare $22.48 not matching the $21.14 charged; "free cancellation until 17:13" already expired when sent at 17:14:45) and is issued only 75 s before trip start, and the fare tables do not reconcile to fix the differential — a textual/eligibility finding the record contradicts, so the case goes to human review. Scope is a surge-differential adjustment (~$3–$6), not the full $4.88 claimed.

element_findings.element: Surge notice stated the new multiplier (SURGE-1)
element_findings.reason: "Fares are 1.4× higher right now" correctly states the new 1.4× multiplier.

element_findings.element: Surge notice stated the revised estimated fare (SURGE-1)
element_findings.reason: Notice gives $22.48 as the new estimated fare; the fare actually charged was $21.14. The stated revised fare does not match the applied fare, so the required item is not properly given.

element_findings.element: Surge notice offered cancellation without penalty (SURGE-1)
element_findings.reason: Notice sent 17:14:45 offers "Free cancellation until 17:13" — an already-expired deadline. No effective option to cancel without penalty was given; the driver's claim of a free-cancel offer is contradicted by the system text.

element_findings.element: Rider notified before or at trip start (SURGE-1)
element_findings.reason: Notice at 17:14:45 is only 75 s before the 17:16:00 start and the chat log contains no rider acknowledgement before riding; notice content is also defective, so the rider did not validly accept the surcharge.

element_findings.element: Whole fare difference attributable solely to surge (SURGE-3)
element_findings.reason: Surge component 0.4 × 14.05 = $5.62 is identifiable, but the quote ($16.26) exceeds quote-base + booking ($15.52) by $0.74 while the rider claims $4.88; the base makeup is not fully reconciled, so the exact differential cannot be fixed mechanically.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver says the app told the rider the new multiplier, new fare and free cancellation. The system notice text contradicts this: the revised fare quoted ($22.48) is not the fare charged ($21.14) and the "free cancellation until 17:13" was already expired when the notice was sent at 17:14:45. System records override statements.

The rider seeks the full $4.88 difference. Only the surge differential is refundable under SURGE-3 (tolls, time fare and booking fee excluded); the exact figure cannot be computed from the unreconciled tables, so the full-difference claim is not granted as pleaded.

ruling.evidence_gap: No needed record is missing, but the record as given is internally unresolved: the notice text's fare and the fare tables do not reconcile (quote $16.26 vs quote-base+booking $15.52; notice fare $22.48 vs charged $21.14), so the SURGE-3 differential cannot be computed deterministically. Escalated on the substantive defect in the notice and the resulting ambiguity, not on a missing file.
